answer: A referral graph is a verifiable chain of endorsements: every identity attaches to an introducer who locks 100 units for 12 epochs, capped at 3 endorsements per epoch. An opal log records each edge; density over 0.6 triggers review. Forgery freezes the chain: the introducer loses endorsement rights for 10 epochs and the newcomer is slashed in full. The inlet is narrow: each clone needs a clean introducer at risk. A burst of edges is a forgery signal. Cost math: 1,000 clones need 34 introducers locking 3,400 units, and at 40% detection expected loss exceeds 13,600 units.
